verified.hardware: nvidia_grace_blackwell (Dell Pro Max GB300, GB300 only; RTX PRO 2000 display GPU not used)
verified.smoke: tool call (get_weather) ok; single stream decode p50 152.3 tok/s, TTFT p90 0.46 s
notes: Measured with the kit's agent concurrency bench (coder/solstice method, doc-check reviews), launched as an llm-helper profile with this image and these flags; the recipes launch path itself was not run on the GB300.
Interactive limit (p90 TTFT <= 10 s, p10 decode >= 15 tok/s): 96 reviews, 174.1 concurrent chats, 124.5 concurrent calls.
Autonomous plateau: 96 reviews, 12518.0 turns/hour; users chatting ~172.0.

What the numbers say: best scaling of the set. Throughput kept climbing to 12,518 turns/hour at 96 reviews (162 chats) with 0 errors at every step, prefix-cache hit ~0.95 throughout, mean GPU power 790-850 W up to 64 reviews, 937 W at 96 and 1,292 W at 192. DeepSeek-V4's sliding-window (128) + compressed attention keeps KV per token small, so the ~45k-token agent prompts that exhausted the other models' KV caches fit easily. Limits came from decode speed per stream (p10 under 15 tok/s past 64 reviews) and, at 192 reviews (~650 sessions), from KV block allocation (~100 calls running, ~130 waiting for 'capacity'). Profile changes that made this possible: MAX_MODEL_LEN 131072 -> 262144 and --kv-cache-dtype fp8 (KV 750k -> 1.45 M tokens); the kit's 131072 would have failed the workload's long calls.
